bar.gross_needed_brl: R$12.218-15.806/month = R$146.600-189.700/yr (fator-r route, fixed stack R$750-1.379/month). RBT12 at the target straddles the R$180.000 faixa boundary, so faixa 2 applies at the top.
bar.blended_tax: Verified at LC 123 (planalto): Anexo III 6,00% to R$180k, 11,20% - R$9.360 above (6,27% at RBT12 R$190k); Anexo V 15,50% to R$180k, 18,00% - R$4.500 above (15,63% at R$190k); §5-J moves Anexo V services to III if folha >= 28% of receita. SPLIT ROUTE (film on III via §5-B XV, stills/design on V via §5-I VI and X), faixa 1-2: HERO (film share 40-65%) 9,3-11,9%; LAUNCH KIT (film 40-50%) 10,8-11,9%; REVISTA (film 18-25%, 4 reels vs 60-90 images) 13,1-14,0%; plus 11% INSS on at least a minimum-wage pro-labore (~R$178/month, minimum wage UNVERIFIED). FATOR-R ROUTE (pro-labore = 28% of RBT12 ~R$3.400-4.400/month, which is part of her take-home anyway): 6,00-6,27% DAS + 3,08% INSS (11% x 28%; 11% derived from Lei 8.212 art. 21 20% less the art. 30 §4 deduction capped at 9%) = 9,08-9,35% on EVERY tier. Fator r is cheaper for LAUNCH KIT and REVISTA, ties/beats HERO unless film > ~60% of the invoice, and removes the UNVERIFIED risk that Receita classes AI-only film as design/publicidade (Anexo V). IRPF on a pro-labore <= R$5.000/month is zero from 2026 (Lei 15.270/2025, per H6C, not re-fetched). Use 9,1-9,4% for all tiers.
bar.stack_cost: Fixed R$750-1.379/month = H6D non-generation stack R$387,11 (Photoshop/Photography plan, CapCut Pro, Canva, ChatGPT Plus, Google One; Frame.io free) + Higgsfield PLUS R$262,68 (1 HERO) or ULTRA R$691,54 (>=2 HEROs or ~4-5 kits, 3.000 credits) incl. Generation inside ULTRA up to 3.000 credits, then R$0,298/credit (18 credits/US$ + IOF). NOT BUDGETED: Higgsfield Enterprise (no-training) for NDA clients, price UNVERIFIED.

supported_price: R$2.500-3.500 per one-product launch set is the most the evidence supports, and it is a CEILING, not a floor: it matches Fabrica's own SP traditional content day (R$1.250-2.500 product-only, R$2.500 for an 80-image day) and Make Move's R$3.000 AI minimum, and sits 2,2-6x above Fabrica's AI a-la-carte equivalent (R$578-1.150) and the in-house replacement (R$500-1.350, H6D). R$5.900 is defensible ONLY where it replaces a human-model shoot with usage rights (lean model shoot R$4.150-7.050 at Fabrica + Job for Model), i.e. ~1/3 of observed launches (5/15, n=15), concentrated in premium DTC brands that already run in-house or agency shoots (Sallve, Dermage); there is zero buyer-side evidence at R$5.900, R$9.900 or R$4.500/revista. At R$2.500-3.500: FLOOR ~US$730/month (2 kits at R$2.500 on the PLUS stack) and ~US$1.435 at 3 kits at R$3.000; CEILING set by the pool, not by hours: at P(external)=33% and a 25% share, R$148,5k/yr = ~US$1.900/month, just under the bar; the hours ceiling (6-11 kits/month at month 18, US$2.900-5.400) binds only if most launching brands buy externally.
treadmill_month24: If self-serve product-lock arrives in 12-18 months (H6D's estimate; Photoroom's Fidelity Layer +9 pp already ships; Higgsfield's brand recipe already composites logos; Adobe Firefly Creative Production reportedly supports 3D digital-twin product fidelity for enterprise - SECONDARY search summary, page returned 503), the guarantee premium goes toward zero. What survives is creative direction + claim check + done-for-you, which the market already prices at R$1.030-1.150 (Fabrica SP, with the client directing), R$1.400-2.900 (ANIMAI 'com direção humana') and R$3.000 (Make Move with beauty direction), against R$500-1.350 in-house. Surviving share of price: 17-51% of a R$5.900 HERO; 50-100% of a R$3.000 LAUNCH KIT (the KIT is already priced near the post-treadmill band, which is the argument for leading with it). Month-24 business at ~R$2.000/set: 6,1-7,9 sets/month, production 24-47 h at 4-6 h/set, ~37-47 active client brands at ~2 buys/yr, ~1,7-2,2 new clients/month x 8-17 h = 14-37 h, total ~43-89 h: borderline on hours, and on the pool it needs 12-16% of the plan-implicit pool (R$1,2M) or 37-48% at P=33% (FAILS). Month 24 = a volume AI studio with origination forever, competing on price with published studios; the claim check is the one residual differentiator and has no observed price anywhere (UNVERIFIED), while CONAR's 2026 guide makes the whole creation chain liable, so it is a liability she carries as well as a feature she sells.
corrections: FABRICA MISREAD: 'não garantindo fidelidade às demais peças' refers to complementary GARMENTS in an apparel studio's AI lookbook, not to packshot labels. Fabrica is not evidence of a label-fidelity gap.

TRADITIONAL ANCHOR OVERSTATED: the same SP studio publishes traditional content production at R$1.250/period (up to 50 treated images or 5 edited videos) and an 80-image day at R$2.500. A lean one-product set is R$1.250-2.500 product-only and R$4.150-7.050 with a model + HMU. H6B's R$9.900-17.000 is the high variant (producer film). R$5.900 is 84-142% of a lean model shoot, not 35-60%. 'Priced against a traditional shoot' therefore supports ~R$2.500-3.500 for product-only launches (8/15 observed) and ~R$4.000-6.000 only for model launches (5/15).
AI-STUDIO BAND: for one SKU it is R$1.030 (Fabrica, computed from its list) to R$3.000 (Make Move minimum), not R$1.400-5.000; R$5.000 is Make Move's 40-garment price.

TAX: H6B's and H6D's floors used a flat 6%. Correct all-in is 9,08-9,35% via fator r (all tiers), or 9,3-11,9% HERO / 10,8-11,9% KIT / 13,1-14,0% REVISTA via the Anexo III/V split plus minimum pro-labore INSS. Fator r dominates for stills-heavy tiers and removes the AI-film classification risk.
H6B FLOOR: '2 HEROs/month = US$2.000' recomputes to R$9.350-9.979 = US$1.805-1.927 at PTAX 5,1795 with the correct tax and an accountant: BELOW the bar. The target needs 2,1-2,7 HEROs/month.
H6D FLOOR: 1 HERO/month = R$4.114-4.314 = US$794-833 (not R$4.350-4.700) once tax is 9,08% and the accountant is in the stack.

STACK: add the accountant (Contweb Simples from R$99,99/month observed; R$250-600 typical, SECONDARY) and the pro-labore INSS. Fixed stack R$750-1.379/month. Higgsfield ULTRA is needed from ~2 HEROs or ~4-5 kits a month.

REVISTA HOURS: CICLO's 15-20 h per 60-90-image pack implies <=10-13 min per finished, composited image; H6D's own steady-state rate (14-28 min/still) gives 19-52 h per pack, so a revista-led desk needs 56-190 h/month at 2,7-3,5 packs. It fits 87 h only if catalogue images take <=~12 min each - stopwatch it.

REVISTA POOL: the 20-brand R$810k pool needs an 18-23% share (edge). Restricted to the beauty/fragrance firms where a label guarantee applies (~12-14 of the 18 named; lingerie/apparel excluded by name, UNVERIFIED), the pool is R$486-567k, pool/4 R$122-142k < the R$147-190k needed: FAILS the market-multiple rule. R$4.500 sits between Fabrica's lookbook-rate (R$1.740-2.090) and campaign-rate (R$4.220-5.810) BOM; which rate a buyer would compare against is UNVERIFIED.

H6A POOL: 'pool is 25-35x revenue, not binding' silently sets P(buys external production at the tier price) to 100%. With the only proxy (5/15 launches used a model shoot), HERO pool/4 is R$292k central (share 12,6-16,2%) and R$110k low (share 34-43%, fails); LAUNCH KIT pool/4 is R$148,5k central, just below the need. Every pool carries 4 stacked multipliers, at least 2 fully unverified: a hypothesis, not a number.

MONTH 3: target volume does not fit 87 h (HERO-only central 84 h with a range to 127; kit-led central 127 h). Realistic month-3 capacity is ~2-3 units. The 12-18-month clock is feasible on hours but is not a month-3 business.
refuted_note: REFUTED AS PRICED: the offer's price anchor ('priced against a traditional shoot') is contradicted by the same SP source's own traditional list, and there is zero buyer-side evidence at R$5.900 or R$4.500. NOT refuted as a business: the structure survives at R$2.500-3.500 per one-product set, and hours fit from ~month 9.
honest_floor_usd_month: US$700-1.500/month at month 12-18 (2-3 one-product sets/month at R$2.500-3.000; R$5.900 HEROs occasional). It reaches US$2.000-2.200 only at ~3,5 units/month of Mix A or 4-5 kits/month at >=R$3.000, which needs ~25-30 active client brands (8-10% of the ~300-brand pool). US$0 if the 20-call price test fails.
verdict_note: Arithmetic works at the plan's prices (2,1-2,7 HEROs or 4,1-5,3 kits a month; 91-94% gross margin; hours fit from ~month 9), but the prices are unsupported: R$2.500-3.500 is the observed ceiling for a one-product set, and at that price the pool clears the market-multiple rule only if most launching brands buy external visuals (unmeasured; the n=15 proxy says ~1/3). The pool-bound ceiling at P=33% is ~US$1.900/month, just under the bar. The treadmill pushes the set toward R$1.500-2.000 by month 24, where it becomes an origination-forever volume studio. Lead with the LAUNCH KIT at R$2.500-3.500 (already near its post-treadmill price), sell the R$5.900 HERO only to replace a model shoot, drop the REVISTA tier unless the stopwatch shows <=12 min per catalogue image and a beauty-only list of >=20 firms is found, and run the 20-call price test (bar committed in advance: >=6/20 name >=R$2.500 external spend per launch) before building anything.
cheapest_next_test: R$0, Portuguese calls: 20 EPP/Demais own-brand hair/skin launchers from the last 14 days of genuinely new ANVISA notifications. One question: 'quanto custou o pacote visual (fotos + vídeo) do último lançamento, e com quem?' Bar committed in advance: >=6/20 name >=R$2.500 of EXTERNAL spend per one-product launch => LAUNCH KIT lives; >=4/20 name >=R$5.000 => HERO lives; <=2/20 at >=R$2.500 => the brand-direct channel is dead at any price above Fabrica's R$1.030. This also measures P(external), the unmeasured multiplier under every pool.
unverified: P(a launching brand buys external campaign production at the tier price): unmeasured; it drives every pool. The only proxy is H6A's n=15 production mix (5 model shoots, 8 product-only/3D, 2 likely AI).

Any buyer-side record of a Brazilian beauty brand paying >= R$2.500 or >= R$5.900 per launch: none found (Workana 403 today; 99Freelas budgets hidden as 'Aberto'; Job for Model has no beauty jobs live; TJSP and Sebraetec PDFs unreachable).
Sales hours per new client (8-17 h): assumes 20-30 calls, 3-5 sample concepts at 1-2 h each and ~1 in 4 samples converting; all UNVERIFIED.
